subject.title: plugins update can downgrade/pin stale plugin version instead of latest available version

question: For targeted plugin id updates with a stale exact npm install record and a newer active plugin copy, should OpenClaw preserve exact-pin semantics with a downgrade guard, or automatically move the plugin to the registry default/latest line?
rationale: Current docs and recent merged work intentionally keep targeted id updates pinned, while this issue's acceptance criteria ask the id form to resolve latest in at least this stale-record scenario.

options.title: Guard Downgrades, Keep Pins
options.body: Preserve documented exact-pin behavior, but fail or skip when the recorded target would downgrade the active plugin and show the explicit package-spec command to move to latest.

options.title: Follow Registry Default
options.body: Change targeted id updates to choose the latest/default registry target when the active plugin is newer than the tracked record, accepting a broader behavior change.

options.title: Keep Current Behavior
options.body: Leave tracked exact specs fully authoritative even when they reactivate an older copy, relying on manual exact package specs for recovery.

recommendation.title: Guard Downgrades, Keep Pins
recommendation.body: Preserve documented exact-pin behavior, but fail or skip when the recorded target would downgrade the active plugin and show the explicit package-spec command to move to latest.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses plugin updater semantics, docs, and update-channel policy where history points to steipete as the strongest routing candidate.
